newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News says HarperCollins abnormal hits net.
newsitem.headline: News says HarperCollins abnormal hits net.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd said on Wednesday its net profit for the year was hit by abnormal losses of A$575 million, mainly due to restructuring its HarperCollins publishing unit.
Sharply lower profits from the book division also affected operating results.

The global media and entertainment group reported a 2.5 percent lift in pre-abnormal net profit to A$1.295 billion in the year to June 30, 1997, which was below market expectations. News Corp said its United Kingdom newspaper, magazines and inserts both exceeded expectations achieving substantial increases over prior year's performance.
The book publishing arm reported sharply lower earnings due to very difficult trading conditions, News Corp said.
The U.S. television results increased operating earnings due to continued growth at the group's original stations, combined with additional contributions newly acquired stations, it said.

News Corp bought 10 TV stations through the acquisition of New World in January 1997. "Lower results at Fox Broadcasting Co (FBC), however, mitigated the impact of these gains resulting in a net operating income increase of four percent for the U.S. Television group," News Corp said in a statement.

In Filmed Entertainment, operating profit was down marginally as compared to a year ago. Twentieth Century Fox began 1996/97 with a successful 'Independence Day', other strong performers were 'Star Wars: Special Edition' trilogy and 'Romeo and Juliet'.
Offsetting these titles were disappointing results from 'Volcano and 'Speed 2', were both released in the June quarter.
News Corp shares closed three cents up at A$5.95 on Tuesday.
